steps.what: Verify tank car, barge or truck numbers against instructions and actual placement

tasks.design: The loader checks the physical vehicle and placement against written instructions in {DOCS} or confirmed verbal directions. A matched number in a system does not establish that the vehicle is physically in the right location.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task connects instructions to physical identity and position.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instructions support the check without assuming machine-readable identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve obscured numbers, changed placement and ambiguous verbal instructions.
tasks.human_edge: Notice the physical mismatch and obtain clarification.

evidence.claim: A warehouse management product exists in the digest, but it does not demonstrate automated physical tank placement verification.

assumptions: No verified position sensor or reliable structured instruction feed is established.
Keep existing document and verbal checks; no new automation upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Availability of readable vehicle identifiers and authoritative placement records
research_questions: How much current checking time could a validated identifier lookup remove after physical inspection remains?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Physical identity and placement verification retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Position loading spouts as cars pass

steps.what: Observe passing cars and position loading spouts at the appropriate times

tasks.design: Retain the loader's direct observation and operation through existing equipment controls in {OPS_SYSTEM}. No new control system or robotic positioning is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Positioning depends on live physical movement and equipment conditions.
tasks.still_hard: Judge alignment and timing under changing conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Maintain situational awareness at the loading point.

evidence.claim: Physical spout positioning is retained; software-only records do not replace live equipment operation.

assumptions: Existing equipment and controls remain unchanged.
No new automation, sensors or maintenance workload is introduced.
unknowns: Current equipment automation and operating arrangements
research_questions: Which positioning actions are already automated by the existing equipment?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Observation and physical positioning remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor tank product movement and coordinate workers to maintain controlled product flow

tasks.design: Keep live flow monitoring and coordination with the loader, using existing {OPS_SYSTEM} indications and {TELEPHONY}. Logging support in the separate record task does not remove this operational attention.
tasks.previous_blocker: Flow continuity depends on physical conditions and coordinated actions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing indications and communication channels support the crew.
tasks.still_hard: Recognize abnormal movement and coordinate a suitable response.
tasks.human_edge: Connect equipment observations with the crew's actual situation.
tasks.altitude: Own coordinated and controlled material movement.

evidence.claim: Recordkeeping software does not establish automatic live tank flow coordination in this design.

assumptions: The loader retains existing observation and response responsibilities.
No new control automation is proposed, so there is no new system upkeep.
Operating log capture is assigned to the separate record task and not claimed as saved monitoring time.
research_questions: Which current coordination delays arise from missing information rather than required live attention?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Monitoring and crew coordination remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Capture products, quantities pumped, gauge readings and operating times from source observations
Record the captured operating event in the configured log
Check operating records and correct discrepancies against original observations

tasks.design: Configure a single operating-event form in the existing {OPS_SYSTEM}; saving the captured fields creates the log without a second transcription. The loader still reads instruments, identifies the product and checks records; no unverified sensor integration or automatic control is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observed readings may be copied into multiple records.
tasks.enabler_now: A native structured form can retain one captured record.
tasks.still_hard: Correctly associate readings, product and transfer event.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a reading or timing discrepancy and investigate it.
tasks.altitude: Own reliable operating records without duplicate transcription.

evidence.claim: Boltrics supplies warehouse management capability; it does not establish tank operating-log functionality or measured savings for this design.
A configured event form can avoid a second transcription after manual observation and capture.

assumptions: The loader produces event ID, tank or vehicle ID, product, quantity, units, gauge value, reading time and operating start/end in s1; its 50 hours includes observation and all manual capture.
The application adds a save timestamp but never substitutes it for a missing observed operating time.
Absent readings, uncertain product identity or offline failure require the current manual record and later reconciliation in s3.
Use the native operating log first; no new sensor feed is assumed.
Six extra focal hours and two other-role hours per 100 baseline hours cover field definitions, reconciliation support and access upkeep.
No saving is claimed from the separate live product-monitoring task.
research_questions: Can one captured event replace duplicate operating entries after checks and upkeep are counted?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75; gross 25 minus 6 focal upkeep gives central net 19%. Pilot range 0-4% discounts the unverified duplication share and physical capture burden; single-entry sites save zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Own accurate loading observations, coordinated product movement and dependable operating records.
reach: Support operations clerks with complete event records
Assist loading coordinators with discrepancy reporting
role.ambitious_version: A loader who records observations once while retaining full attention to physical identity, equipment position and product movement.
